requirements.statement: The server exposes one anonymous, read-only desktop bootstrap v1 response that exactly matches the frozen client schema and declares every not-yet-implemented capability as false.
acceptance: GET /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap returns HTTP 200, application/json and the exact closed v1 response without authentication.
The response contains no account, credential, cookie, device code, refresh token, price, wallet URL or backend configuration.
All six future capability flags remain false and repeated or concurrent reads remain equivalent.
Unsupported methods do not mutate state and a subsequent valid GET still returns the recognized response.
No database schema, migration, payment, deployment or existing API behavior changes in this release unit.

requirements.statement: The server exposes a versioned desktop v2 integration that lets a desktop client obtain a dedicated revocable session through explicit first-party browser approval and then read truthful account, usage, available-model, pricing, billing-comparison and wallet-link projections without adding database schema or handling payment inside the desktop API.
acceptance: The immutable v1 bootstrap remains unchanged while /api/desktop/v2/bootstrap advertises only implemented v2 capabilities and keeps tool_keys_manage false.
A device code is stored only in Redis for five minutes, must be approved by a live browser session, is polling-rate limited and can issue at most one desktop session.
Desktop refresh-token rotation and logout reuse existing user_sessions; refresh secrets are returned only to the desktop exchange/refresh caller and are never placed in a URL or log.
Authenticated read endpoints derive account, usage, models and pricing from the same existing owners used by the web dashboard and expose no prompt or response content.

Billing comparison uses the same consume-log cohort for site and reconstructed official cost, fixed USD/CNY 6.75, excludes non-comparable subscription records, and reports coverage instead of fabricating savings.
The wallet endpoint returns only the first-party /wallet/ URL and the desktop API does not accept payment details or payment callbacks.
No model, migration, database schema, deployment, Nginx or production configuration file changes belong to this release unit.
